class.name: NNBTParallel
class.brief_description: Ticks all its enabled child nodes and combines their statuses using [member success_policy] and [member failure_policy]. [code]RUNNING[/code] takes precedence over a combined [code]FAILURE[/code], which takes precedence over [code]SUCCESS[/code].
class.description:
The parallel node ticks every enabled child node, regardless of child order, and never early-exits. Disabled children are not ticked and are excluded from every count.
[code]SKIP[/code] results count as [code]SUCCESS[/code] for the policy evaluation. [code]SKIP[/code] never caused a failure and a lone [code]SKIP[/code] child returned [code]SUCCESS[/code], so the default policies reproduce the historical behaviour exactly.
After ticking every enabled child the node computes: [codeblock] if any child returned RUNNING: result = RUNNING else: success_met = success_policy == REQUIRE_ALL ? num_success == num_enabled : num_success > 0 failure_met = failure_policy == REQUIRE_ALL ? num_failure == num_enabled : num_failure > 0 if success_met and failure_met: result = FAILURE elif success_met: result = SUCCESS elif failure_met: result = FAILURE else: result = FAILURE [/codeblock] The precedence is therefore [code]RUNNING[/code], then the both-met [code]FAILURE[/code] tie (which matches the historical failure-before-success behaviour), then [code]SUCCESS[/code], then [code]FAILURE[/code]. The final [code]FAILURE[/code] is the documented fallback for mixed outcomes under [constant SUCCESS_REQUIRE_ALL] and [constant FAILURE_REQUIRE_ALL], where neither policy is satisfied.
The defaults ([constant SUCCESS_REQUIRE_ALL] and [constant FAILURE_REQUIRE_ONE]) reproduce the original matrix: any [code]RUNNING[/code] child returns [code]RUNNING[/code], otherwise any [code]FAILURE[/code] child returns [code]FAILURE[/code], otherwise the node returns [code]SUCCESS[/code].
An empty parallel, or one whose children are all disabled, has no enabled children. "Require all" is then trivially true and "require one" is false, so the node returns [code]SUCCESS[/code] only with [constant SUCCESS_REQUIRE_ALL] and [constant FAILURE_REQUIRE_ONE]; every other policy combination returns [code]FAILURE[/code].

members.member: How many enabled children must return [code]FAILURE[/code] for the parallel node to fail. [constant FAILURE_REQUIRE_ONE] (default) fails when at least one enabled child fails; [constant FAILURE_REQUIRE_ALL] fails only when every enabled child fails. Values outside the [enum FailurePolicy] range are rejected with a single engine error that names [code]set_failure_policy[/code], the received value and the valid range; the previous policy is kept.

How many enabled children must return [code]SUCCESS[/code] (or [code]SKIP[/code], which counts as a success) for the parallel node to succeed. [constant SUCCESS_REQUIRE_ALL] (default) requires every enabled child to succeed; [constant SUCCESS_REQUIRE_ONE] requires at least one. Values outside the [enum SuccessPolicy] range are rejected with a single engine error that names [code]set_success_policy[/code], the received value and the valid range; the previous policy is kept.

constants.constant: The parallel node returns [code]SUCCESS[/code] only when every enabled child succeeded. This is the default.
The parallel node returns [code]SUCCESS[/code] when at least one enabled child succeeded.
The parallel node returns [code]FAILURE[/code] when at least one enabled child failed. This is the default.
The parallel node returns [code]FAILURE[/code] only when every enabled child failed.
